answer: In an island marketplace, each agent must lock a refundable bond before bidding for tasks; a cipher verifies that bids and any proven rule violations belong to that bonded key. To reach the summit of influence with a thousand fake agents, an attacker must lock a thousand bonds, tying up capital and risking forfeiture for proven abuse. The scheme makes identities costly, not impossible, and cannot distinguish a wealthy attacker from many honest agents.
